readback.name: Poincare.MetricRescaleScalarGradient.constSMul_scalarGradNormSqAt
readback.mathematical_statement: For any natural dimension n and any Hausdorff smooth boundaryless n-dimensional charted space M carrying the supplied smooth Riemannian metric g, let c be a fixed positive real number and let cg be the metric with fiber inner product c times that of g. Assuming the recorded C1 regularity instances for both canonical Levi-Civita connections, at every x in M the squared cg-norm of the cg-gradient of the scalar curvature of cg equals c^(-3) times the squared g-norm of the g-gradient of the scalar curvature of g. Here gradient is specifically the inverse metric applied to the repository exterior derivative of the scalar-curvature function, and the norm square is its pairing with the metric. This is constant positive rescaling; it does not concern a spatially varying conformal factor or a time-dependent flow. The name of the metric type imposes smoothness and positive definiteness, but this exact theorem has no compactness or connectedness hypothesis.
